_comment: Host manifest for lib/Scythe.Rules/Linting against data/detection_signatures.json. Read by lib/Scythe.Rules.Tests/Linting/ShippedSignatureFileTests.cs (dotnet test) and usable with LintTool --manifest. Two things are deliberately NOT listed here because the test derives them from the engine source and they cannot go stale: which sets are consumed (every Get-Sig / Join-AllowRegex call site whose loader variable is used somewhere) and which are allowlists (every Join-AllowRegex name). Only what the source cannot reveal - how the host MATCHES an entry - lives here. Classify a new set by reading its consumer, never by its name.
_comment_allowlists: Sets that suppress or skip a detection without going through Join-AllowRegex: -contains / -notin skip lists, the script's own-strings self-filter, the partner-vendor list, and the two regex skip lists phase 147/159 pass to Test-ScytheNameRule.
_comment_literal_sets: Matched as escaped SUBSTRINGS: [regex]::Escape($_) inside -match, or bounded the same way (c2_pipe_patterns). The linter escapes these before compiling and runs the collision corpus on the escaped form - the same substring match the engine performs, which is why an entry here may not be a word that occurs inside a legitimate process name. A regex set listed here loses every regex check, so add a name ONLY after reading its consumer.
_comment_equality_sets: Compared as WHOLE values: -contains / -in / -eq, a hashtable key, a mutex name opened by exact name, or a path expanded and handed to Test-Path / Get-Item. Checked as ^escaped$, so '.bat' in an extension list does not collide with 'Adobe Acrobat' and a path list is not a detection an allowlist can swallow.
_comment_wildcard_sets: -like globs, or paths carrying a * segment for Get-Item. The engine builds '^' + [regex]::Escape($_).Replace('\*','.*') + '$' from them and so does the linter.
_comment_reference_sets: Entries that name legitimate or structural things BY DESIGN: the system image names a masquerade check compares against, LOLBin and auto-elevate binaries, the child processes remote execution spawns, file extensions, kill-chain stage keywords matched against the tool's own finding text, and the dual-use tunnelling tools whose second list exists precisely to downgrade them. 'This matches real software' is the point. Compile, budget and duplicate checks still apply; the collision corpus, the length floor and the swallowed-detection pairing do not.
_comment_substring_allowlists: Allowlists matched against text whose LOCATION the attacker does not choose (install paths, signer names) - CLAUDE.md's 'path-only allowlists are fine' rule. They are held to component anchoring (an entry begins and ends at a path separator or a real anchor) at warning level instead of ^...$ at error level. Every allowlist NOT listed here is compared against an attacker-chosen value (a run-key value, a command line, a service or file name, an account) and must be fully anchored. Two entries here are weaker than the rest and are recorded, not hidden: trusted_root_ca_issuers matches bare vendor words against root-store certificate subjects, which a rogue CA can name itself after, and native_messaging_benign_hosts matches host-name PREFIXES that an attacker registering a host can also choose. Both are heuristic by design and belong to the FP/hardening round (HANDOFF.md 2026-09-02).
_comment_accepted_collisions: Collisions with the legitimate-software corpus that were reviewed and kept. Reported at Info with the reason; editing the entry re-opens the question.

accepted_collisions.why: impacket's psexec/smbexec drop an 8-random-letter service binary and the shape is the only signal. The rule runs only over *.exe CREATED in System32 inside the scan window, at POSSIBLE with FixAction Info, so it is never auto-selected. Any 8-letter Windows binary (msconfig.exe, cleanmgr.exe, taskkill.exe) matches by shape on a machine serviced inside the window: expected noise for the FP round, not an action.
